chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the vessels of the Ahl al-Zimma and the Magians, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat in their vessels, nor from their food which they cook, nor in their vessels in which they drink wine.'

key_terms.أهل الذمة: People under covenant/responsibility (non-Muslims living in Islamic lands)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating from the vessels of non-Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), distinguishing between general food consumption and specific vessel usage to preserve ritual purity and identity. The prohibition extends to vessels used for wine, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on avoiding *khamr* (intoxicants) and maintaining distinct communal boundaries with *Ahl al-Kitab* and *Magians*. This hadith serves as a foundational text for fiqh discussions on *istihlak* (dissolution) and the permissibility of eating from non-Muslims' utensils after washing.
